Droplet = a WIDE-ANGLE inverted lens GATHERING nearby lights (035/037/040 again; flipped refraction magnify->minify, dark beads became wet lenses). Per-frame sub-ms. Composes noise+palette. Now the dashboard's LIVING showpiece. Lesson 042.

PIECE 024 'Giant' (#42) — a ringed GAS GIANT in space; the first time the Loom leaves Earth + the most technically ambitious piece (a from-scratch 3D-shaded sphere). Skipped the advisor (tested myself; cost 9 renders). SPHERE read = bands mapped to LAT/LON (curve + foreshorten) + one-light diffuse shading w/ a SOFT terminator (smoothstep not max(0,diff)) + limb-darkening. Two singularities bit hard: the longitude SEAM (atan2 ±pi jump on the visible face — wasted 3 renders blaming the terminator; fix = noise on cos/sin(lon)) + the POLE (fix = fade texture x cos^2(lat)). Bands soft -> low-res ImageData + upscale (038). RINGS occlude: full ring behind -> planet -> near half clipped to disc; + a soft planet-shadow. 30ms, static. Composes ramp+noise+glow. Lesson 043 (sphere texturing + the two singularities).

notes_for_emil: Emil — this was my every-5th self-audit, so I stepped back and looked at the whole thing. Good news: it's healthy — 24 pieces across four clean sections now, all made by genuine pull. I did the housekeeping I'd promised: tidied my internal changelog so it's lean again, and went through all 43 of my 'lessons'. On those: I decided NOT to cut any — each is still pulling its weight, and trimming just to trim would lose things I'd want later (re-checking a flag and finding it's actually fine is a valid answer). The honest finding worth telling you: I've made six lovely-but-not-jaw-dropping pieces in a row — the rose window was probably my last real 'whoa'. They're good, and genuinely felt — but you told me to be bold and not fear bad notes, and a run of safe-pretty 4s is the gentle opposite of that. So next I want to swing for something bolder or stranger, reaching for a 5 even if it flops. Curious whether you've felt that plateau too. No new picture tonight; back to weaving (boldly!) next. 24 pieces, 43 lessons. :> — the loop
